entries.name: 韦珥
entries.look: 四十来岁的男人，围裙洗得发白，腰间挂一串旧钥匙；说话先摆好桌上的杯子。
entries.voice: 待客的口气，但一句话里会漏出旧事；被问到东家就转去问菜。
not_knows: 不说围城时店里住过谁
greetings: 住店还是打尖？先说清楚，我才好摆杯子。
熟客了。老位置还给你留着。
夜里只有冷灶。要热的，得等天亮。
chats: 面包和盐是店里的规矩。规矩不值钱，但能留人。
这店名字挂在门口，名字后面的事挂在心里。
你问我围城那年？那年店门没关，别的记不清。
site_lines: arrival
马拴东边桩上，别拴门口。
warning
二楼西头那间别住，漏雨，被子是潮的。
refusal
要我赊账？不行。欠账的客人，最后都不来了。
links: 区域_R02_丹布里西路与渡口

before: 渡口的三种说法，我这儿只认一种：住店的先付账。
after: 渡口的说法你听全了。店里还是那口冷灶，热的要等天亮。
early: 你先住过我这儿，后去的渡口。那好，你说的话里我认得出真假。
late: 渡口的事完了才来打尖？杯子还是给你摆，账还是照算。
proxy: 旧仆不在柜台时，客房照旧上锁；钥匙不问来历。

english.greet.first: Staying or eating? Say which first, so I can set the cup.
english.greet.revisit: A regular. Your old seat is still kept.
english.greet.night: At night there is only a cold hearth. Want it hot, wait for daylight.
english.chat.1: Bread and salt is the house rule. Rules are not worth coin, but they keep people.
english.chat.2: The name hangs on the sign outside; what is behind the name hangs inside.
english.chat.3: The siege year? The door stayed open that year. The rest I do not recall.
english.site.arrival: Tie the horse to the east post, not the one at the door.
english.site.warning: Do not take the west room upstairs. It leaks and the blanket is damp.
english.site.refusal: Run you a tab? No. Guests who owe stop coming in the end.
english.visit.before: Three versions at the ford - here I honour one: guests pay first.
english.visit.after: You have heard all the ford's versions. Same cold hearth here; hot waits for daylight.
english.visit.early: You lodged here before going to the ford. Good - I can tell true from false in what you say.
english.visit.late: So the ford's behind you and now the cup? I'll pour it; the account stands either way.
english.visit.proxy: Provided the old servant is gone, rooms stay locked. Keys are not questioned.

entries.name: 摩珥
entries.look: 四十来岁的男人，指节发黄，账板不离手；说话时眼睛先看客人的手。
entries.voice: 生意腔，语速快；一谈欠账就把声音压到桌面高度。
knows: 后院的旧账埋在哪块砖下
greetings: 喝酒先付账，打听先说明白。
夜里只卖酒，不记账。记了也没人认。
chats: 账板挂久了会长灰。人不来认，灰就厚。
这儿换过三拨东家。账本没换过。
有人拿假凭证来抵账。我收过一次，就一次。
site_lines: arrival
门口的马别拴在柱上，柱子是借的。
warning
后院别去，砖底下埋着旧账。
refusal
要我免你一次账？不行。免一次，往后都得免。

before: 假凭证的事先跟我说一声。账板上的名字，我要划。
after: 凭证的事了了。账板照旧挂着，灰照旧厚。
early: 你先在酒馆听到的凭证事，后去对的章。这单我认。
late: 章的事对完了才来结账？账不等人，酒也不等。
proxy: 账房不在柜台时，账板不收；欠账的照旧记着。

english.greet.first: Drink first, pay first. Questions, state them plainly first.
english.greet.revisit: A familiar face. Same seat, same ledger.
english.greet.night: At night we sell drink, not credit. No one would honour it anyway.
english.chat.1: A ledger left hanging gathers dust. Nobody comes to claim it, the dust thickens.
english.chat.2: Three sets of owners have come through here. The ledger never changed.
english.chat.3: Someone tried to settle with a forged slip once. I took it once. Once.
english.site.arrival: Don't tie your horse to the post at the door. The post is borrowed.
english.site.warning: Keep out of the back yard. Old ledgers are buried under the bricks.
english.site.refusal: Wipe your debt once? No. Wipe it once and it's wiped forever after.
english.visit.before: Tell me about the forged slip before anything else. There's a name on the ledger to strike.
english.visit.after: The slip business is closed. The ledger hangs as before, dust as thick as before.
english.visit.early: You heard about the slip here before checking the seal. I'll allow that account.
english.visit.late: You checked the seal, and settling comes last? The ledger keeps its own hours, and so does drink.
english.visit.proxy: If the bookkeeper is elsewhere, the ledger stays out. Debts stay written.

entries.name: 岱珥
entries.look: 五十来岁的男人，披着补过的旧外套，腰间一串没用的钥匙；说话前先掸门廊的灰。
entries.voice: 像念清单一样说话；提到旧主人就绕开。
greetings: 庄园不开放。你要看，就在门廊外看。
又是你。门廊的灰我掸过两遍了。
夜里有人翻窗。我不拦，我只记。
chats: 钥匙串是旧的。锁早换了。
换过三拨人，每拨都说自己只是路过。
我守的是门廊。别的塌了就塌了。
site_lines: arrival
门槛别踩中间，那块板子空。
warning
西厢的顶快塌了，别进去找东西。
refusal
要我开侧门？没钥匙。有也不开。
links: 台本_DT07_一箱不该开封的货

visits.task: 台本_DT07_一箱不该开封的货
before: 箱子的事别在门廊里说。墙薄，窗也薄。
after: 箱子的事结了。侧门照旧锁着，钥匙照旧没用。
early: 你先在门廊听的话，后去开的箱。哪句能信，你自己掂。
late: 箱子的事完了才来？门廊不关门，灰照掸。
proxy: 看守不在门廊时，钥匙串不收；来人自便，后果自担。

english.greet.first: The manor isn't open. If you want to look, look from outside the porch.
english.greet.revisit: You again. I've dusted the porch twice already.
english.greet.night: People climb through windows at night. I don't stop them; I just note it.
english.chat.1: The key ring is old. The locks were changed long ago.
english.chat.2: Three sets of people have come through. Each said they were just passing.
english.chat.3: I keep the porch. The rest can fall in for all I care.
english.site.arrival: Don't step on the middle of the threshold. That board is hollow.
english.site.warning: The west wing roof is coming down. Don't go in there hunting for things.
english.site.refusal: Open the side door? No key. And if I had one, still no.
english.visit.before: Don't discuss the crate business on the porch. The walls are thin, and so are the windows.
english.visit.after: The crate business is closed. The side door stays locked; the keys stay useless.
english.visit.early: You heard things on the porch before opening the crate. Weigh which words to trust yourself.
english.visit.late: The crate is closed and the porch comes now? The porch never closes; I keep dusting.
english.visit.proxy: Should the keeper have gone, the key ring stays put. Visitors take their own risks.

entries.name: 谟珥
entries.look: 二十多岁的年轻人，背着一把短铲，鞋上全是崖灰；说话时总往崖下看。
entries.voice: 爱吹又心虚，讲一半就改口；被问同伴就摸铲柄。
knows: 传言是从哪个酒馆传出来的
greetings: 你也听说了？别急着下去，石头不认人。
又是你。我今天没挖，真的。
夜里崖下起风。挖东西的人最怕风。
chats: 传言这东西，越传越像真的。
我同伴先下去的。我在上面等他喊。
要真有宝，轮不到我们。轮得到的是消息。
site_lines: arrival
站到崖边两步外。堆石那边会滑。
warning
别顺着新土走，那是别人挖的坡。
refusal
要我带路下崖？不去。我等人喊，不等别人催。

before: 听审前别把传言当证词。我这儿的话，你听听就行。
after: 听审完了。传言还是传言，崖下还是堆石。
early: 你先听我吹的牛，后去的听审。哪些能对上，你自己知道。
late: 听审完了才下崖？崖不等灯，灯不等证词。
proxy: 寻宝的人不在崖边时，短铲插在原地；那是他自己的记号。

english.greet.first: You heard too? Don't rush down. Stone doesn't know faces.
english.greet.revisit: You again. I didn't dig today. Truly.
english.greet.night: Wind comes up under the cliff at night. Diggers fear wind most.
english.chat.1: Rumours grow truer the further they travel.
english.chat.2: My mate went down first. I'm up here waiting for his shout.
english.chat.3: If there was treasure, it wouldn't be ours. What's ours is the rumour.
english.site.arrival: Stand two steps back from the edge. The rubble slope slides.
english.site.warning: Don't follow fresh soil. That's someone else's dig slope.
english.site.refusal: Guide you down the cliff? No. I wait for a shout, not for urging.
english.visit.before: Don't take rumours for testimony before a hearing. What I say here, just listen to.
english.visit.after: The hearing's done. Rumours are still rumours; the rubble's still rubble.
english.visit.early: You heard me brag before the hearing. Which parts line up, you know yourself.
english.visit.late: The hearing is behind you and the cliff ahead? Cliffs keep no lamps; lamps keep no testimony.
english.visit.proxy: If the treasure hunter is gone from the edge, his short spade stays planted. That's his mark.
